clue.text: Corrupt rep who's in possession

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted from its proper form, so these words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: short for who is, giving the letters W, H, O, S

explanation.surface: A dishonest sales rep is caught holding stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges REP, WHOS and IN, nine letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of having something as your own, a synonym for possession.

clue.text: The Sound of Music lacks a bit of verve

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an oompah is the sound of a brass band, so a sound of music
a single letter A, a small bit

explanation.surface: Someone finds the famous musical film lacking energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics point to the film, but read it as a description: an oompah is a sound of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph means energy or vigour, which is what verve is.

clue.text: Lunatic, off his trolley, completely unable to start composition

parts.note: a nut is a lunatic
off one's trolley means crazy, and so does crackers

indicators.note: unable to start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: quite means completely

explanation.surface: A madman, utterly deranged, cannot begin writing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unable to start' drops the Q from QUITE, leaving UITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nutcracker Suite is a musical work by Tchaikovsky, so a composition.

clue.text: In principle, small! person receiving small amount of cash…

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a runt is a small person
a dime is a ten-cent coin, a small sum

explanation.surface: In theory, a tiny person is given a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word; 'small!' with its exclamation pairs with 'person' to mean a tiny one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a basic principle or element of a subject.

clue.text: … worried whether I might be accompanying this …

indicators.note: worried means disturbed or shaken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously wonders whether they might be coming along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges WHETHER I.
explanation.definitionFit: Herewith is a formal word meaning with this, as enclosed in a letter.

clue.text: . grant, to rearrange it

parts.note: to perm is to permute, to arrange in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be allowed to reorganize something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearrange' looks like an anagram signal but there is no fodder: it is PERM.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to grant permission or allow.

clue.text: Fanatical artist made an offer

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
to bid is to make an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A painter at an auction gets carried away with bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means fanatical or extreme in one's views, a figurative use of the word for a mad dog.

clue.text: Perhaps criminal assistant employed by bishop

indicators.note: employed by is read as working within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A bishop's helper may be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishops are styled Right Reverend, hence the crossword abbreviation for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider attacks or robs, so a criminal is one example.

clue.text: A squabble -— bunked off for something to eat

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a quarrel someone ran away to get food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges A SQUABBLE BUNKED; BUBBLE AND SQUEAK is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is a British fried dish, so food.

clue.text: To belittle is wrong, dead wrong

indicators.note: wrong here means badly placed, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists it is totally mistaken to disparage another.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'wrong' rearranges WRONG and DEAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: To downgrade someone is to lower their status, to belittle them.

clue.text: Swordsman who is middle-of-the road, somewhat subdued

indicators.note: subdued is read as held under, so one piece is kept down inside the other

parts.note: MOR is the radio abbreviation for middle-of-the-road music
a tad means somewhat, a little

explanation.surface: A fencer is described as moderate in his views and rather quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subdued' puts A TAD inside MOR, the music-radio label for middle-of-the-road.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull with a sword, so a swordsman of the ring.

clue.text: In this array of colours there's a brown I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine or invent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots a brown band among the colours of a spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges A BROWN I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is an arc showing the spectrum of colours in order.

clue.text: Concubines make you run a mile

parts.note: to hare is to run fast
M is the abbreviation for one mile

explanation.surface: A sultan's wives send a suitor fleeing a mile away.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives and concubines in a Muslim household.

clue.text: Like snow drop, but give up carrying it

parts.note: snow is white
to flag is to droop or drop with tiredness

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a snowdrop, then gives up on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snow drop' looks like the flower snowdrop; split it into two clue pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A white flag is the banner of surrender, so one carries it to signal giving up.

clue.text: Half a dozen in hiding in large town's environs

parts.note: half a dozen is six, VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: hiding in means concealed within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Six people are lying low somewhere around a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a piece; the second belongs to the container signal 'hiding in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The vicinity is the surrounding area, the same idea as environs.

clue.text: Very exultant about books I discuss in public

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: elate is an old adjective meaning exultant
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about books shares views openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' is a single-letter abbreviation, and 'I' stays as the letter itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate a matter is to air it, discussing it openly.

clue.text: Grand Commander is slightly crazy

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an aga is an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: A senior officer is said to be a bit unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for mildly mad or senile.

clue.text: Flower garden in a pit

definitions.meaning: a formal garden of ornamental flower beds
the ground floor area of a theatre behind the orchestra

explanation.surface: A flower garden is placed in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: In the theatre a parterre is the area at the back of the ground floor, the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Parterre names both a formal patterned garden and the rear stalls of a theatre.

clue.text: President uses ceremonial language that's artificial and posh

parts.note: pomp means ceremonial display
Ido is an invented language derived from Esperanto
U means upper class, from the U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: A head of state speaks a stilted, pompous, upper-class tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Pompidou was President of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompidou was President of France from 1969 to 1974.

clue.text: Shortage of work, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to knead is to work dough with the hands

explanation.surface: There is said to be a lack of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Need means a lack or want of something, as does shortage.

clue.text: Crowd around ill-gotten gains

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around
boodle is slang for money got by bribery or graft

explanation.surface: A mob gathers round some stolen loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is not a container here: it is CA, circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle means a lot or crowd, as in the whole kit and caboodle.

clue.text: Practically nothing put into charitable collection that's just started

indicators.note: put into says this piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: alms are gifts to the poor
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: just started means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Hardly anything has been given to a charity appeal that has only just begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' puts O inside ALMS, and 'just started' takes T from 'that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means practically or nearly.

clue.text: Members don't sit in this alcove

definitions.meaning: a break in parliamentary sittings when members are away
a niche set back in a wall

explanation.surface: MPs take a break in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage MPs are Members, and a recess is the holiday when parliament does not sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Recess means both a parliamentary break and an alcove or niche.

clue.text: Broke in thus, having left opening

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Someone broke in this way, using a gap on one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' reads as a past-tense verb with 'in', but it is the adjective, short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay debts, which is what being broke means.

clue.text: Ill feeling produced by curtailment of game

indicators.note: curtailment means cutting off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two players

explanation.surface: Resentment arises when a game is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailment of' drops the final T of PIQUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is resentment from wounded pride, a form of ill feeling.

clue.text: Ancient articles from Europe

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
der is the German word for the

explanation.surface: Old pieces of writing come from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder means older, so ancient compared with others.

clue.text: Bill and I pass ourselves off as fatty

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster
to pose as something is to pass oneself off as it

explanation.surface: Two people pretend to be overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means consisting of or relating to fat, so fatty.

clue.text: Duck in ginger offered to chief

parts.note: ginger as a hair colour is red
the head is the chief person

explanation.surface: A cook serves duck with ginger to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The redhead is a North American diving duck; 'ginger' tempts as a cooking ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: The redhead is a species of North American duck with a reddish head.

clue.text: Choose to deliver only part of the lecture

indicators.note: only part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A speaker decides to give just some of the talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Choose to deliver' as the definition, but 'to deliver' belongs to the surface link; 'Choose' alone gives the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose, especially by voting.

clue.text: Being happy exploring caves, and braver, the Spanish went in, I came out

indicators.note: went in says this piece enters the other
came out says this letter leaves the word

parts.note: spunky means plucky, so spunkier is braver
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys potholing, and a bolder Spaniard went in while I left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun, a creature, so the definition is the whole opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A spelunker is a cave explorer, a person who enjoys exploring caves.
